deep.reconstruction:
Authorship and date. Despite the bundle name, this page is not by Riemann. It continues a letter dated Göttingen, 18 January 1876, ten years after Riemann's death. The letter criticises the proof sheets (Bogen 19, pp. 289–304) of Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's posthumous memoir on minimal surfaces, 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', for the 1876 Gesammelte Werke. The writer had just moved to Göttingen, teaches 13 hours a week, has privileged access to Weierstrass's unpublished formulas, and treats minimal surfaces as a specialist. Almost certainly this is H. A. Schwarz writing to Heinrich Weber, co-editor of the Werke, who had just moved to Königsberg ('in K.'). The mathematics is editorial criticism of Riemann's printed argument, not new research.

Content, step by step.

(a) Pp. 290–292: minor wording points. A 'squared line element' is improper usage. 'sind daher' should be repeated on p. 291. A transition is missing after equation 8 on p. 292.

(b) P. 293: Riemann/Hattendorff write log X = 2 log Y + (continuous function). Context (my reconstruction, consistent with Riemann's method): x, y, z are the coordinates of the minimal surface. X, Y, Z are holomorphic functions of the form coordinate + i·(conjugate harmonic coordinate). They are fixed only up to additive purely imaginary constants, and satisfy dX^2 + dY^2 + dZ^2 = 0. Schwarz lists two gaps.

(1) The imaginary constants must be normalised so that X = Y = 0 at the chosen point x = y = z = 0. Otherwise the relation has no meaning.

(2) The text never says where Y comes from. Schwarz supplies the missing argument. The coordinate system is chosen with the x-axis along the surface normal at the origin, so the surface is a graph x = f(y, z) with f and grad f vanishing at 0. The minimal surface equation is
(1+f_z^2) f_yy − 2 f_y f_z f_yz + (1+f_y^2) f_zz = 0.
Neglecting higher-order terms it reduces to Laplace's equation f_yy + f_zz = 0. Hence, to first order, the plane coordinates y, z are isothermal and one may take Y = y + i z. For the plane x = 0 exactly one has Y = y + iz and Z = z − iy, giving dY^2 + dZ^2 = 0 and X constant (= 0).

Consequence (implicit; mine). x vanishes to second order at the origin. So X, holomorphic in Y, has a zero of order 2 when the zero is simple-curvature generic: X = c·Y^2·(1 + O(Y)), i.e. log X − 2 log Y is continuous. The same gap recurs on p. 295. Why does arg Y change by 2π around the point? The marginal note says p. 289's formula does not give this. With X ~ c·Y^2, one circuit (arg Y increases by 2π) makes arg X increase by 4π.

(c) P. 294, two corrections. First, 'wirklich herfallen' (reading uncertain) is unjustified, since the turning points of the normals are not known. Second, the spherical (Gauss) image of a straight boundary segment is not a great circle but an arc of a great circle: normals along a line are perpendicular to it. The claim 'arg X changes by nπ' holds only if the imaginary part of X is also normalised to vanish at the origin; likewise on p. 295.

(d) P. 301: calling the formulas 'complete' is presumptuous. They can be made more complete by eliminating the 2A + B constants used to remove the logarithmic terms. Weierstrass possesses such formulas.
errors: Not an error of mathematics but of attribution: the page is from an 1876 letter (very likely H. A. Schwarz to H. Weber) about Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir, not a Riemann manuscript.
Schwarz's points are valid criticisms of the printed text: missing normalisation of the imaginary integration constants, missing justification of Y ≈ y + iz, and great circle vs. arc of great circle.

Schwarz's own sketch is first-order only. Strictly, log X = 2 log Y + continuous also needs X to have a zero of exactly order 2 at the point (nonvanishing second-order term). He leaves this implicit; it is presumably guaranteed by the setting in Riemann's text.

results.what: Linearisation of the minimal surface equation at a point with normal along the x-axis gives Laplace's equation; hence Y ≈ y + iz to first order
results.modern_name: Linearised minimal surface equation; local isothermal coordinates / Weierstrass–Enneper setup

results.what: Normalisation of additive imaginary constants so that X = Y = 0 at the point; then X ~ c Y^2 and log X − 2 log Y is continuous, and arg X winds twice as fast as arg Y
results.modern_name: Order of zero of a holomorphic function / local behaviour of conjugate minimal surface coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's memoir (ed. Hattendorff 1867), commented by Schwarz

results.what: Gauss image of a straight boundary segment of a minimal surface lies on an arc of a great circle
results.modern_name: Schwarz reflection / Gauss map along straight lines

results.what: Remark that Weierstrass had formulas for polygonal Plateau problems free of the constants used to cancel logarithmic terms
results.modern_name: Weierstrass's treatment of the Plateau problem for polygons

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an 1876 editorial letter (almost certainly Schwarz to Weber) criticising Hattendorff's edition of Riemann's published minimal-surface memoir. It contains only routine first-order arguments and editorial corrections, and nothing new attributable to Riemann.

transcription_corrections: Heading context: the 'previous page' date 1876 and the content show this is a letter about Hattendorff's edition, not Riemann's own text. Metadata should not attribute it to Riemann.
'wirklich herfallen' and 'Umkehrpunkte der Normalen' are uncertain readings. The image is ambiguous ('Umkehrpunkte' could be another compound), so these should be kept flagged.
Struck-out phrase before the quotation reads roughly 'Etwas Ähnliches ist folgendes gemeint'; the exact wording is uncertain, but it is deleted in the manuscript.
The PDE in the image is written as ∂²x/∂y² + ∂²x/∂z² = 0 (x as function of y, z); the transcription is correct in substance.
